name: Kedleston Hall

dates.altered: The entry adds 'Interiors complete by the 1780s.'
dates.note: The listed-building entry prints '1758-65 by Matthew Brettingham, James Paine and Robert Adam'. The registered park-and-garden entry 1000451 tells the same sequence differently: Brettingham engaged 1758, superseded by Paine before the end of 1759, Adam taking over by April 1760, 'Work was completed in 1765'. Both are recorded; neither is resolved.

quotes.text: SK 34 SW PARISH OF KEDLESTON KEDLESTON PARK 3/41 Kedleston Hall 25.9.51 GV I Large country house, set in large landscape park. 1758-65 by Matthew Brettingham, James Paine and Robert Adam. Interiors complete by the 1780s.
quotes.page: Official list entry 1311507, Details, entry header and opening sentence

quotes.text: Red brick faced in ashlar and render. Hipped Welsh slate roofs. Various brick stacks largely hidden within the roof wells.
Main rectangular block with quadrant colonnades and rectangular pavilions following Palladio's Villa Mocenigo. Rusticated basement, piano nobile and attic storeys.
Principal north front: Centre block of eleven bays. Hexastyle, giant Corinthian portico over a basement of five round arches. Three statues on the pediment. Double staircase.
Three bays on either side of the portico with square sash windows to the basement, glazing bar sashes in pedimented aedicules above and rectangular attic windows with moulded surrounds.

Linked to identical pavilions, lower than the main block but still with basement, piano nobile and attic storeys. The upper storeys are cement rendered. Five bays, with four attached Ionic columns supporting a pediment.
South front of 3-3-3 bays. The centre piece derived from the Arch of Constantine. Four detached Corinthian columns standing close to the antae and pilasters against the wall.
